mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4.5% in the month prior to the decision date is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions dampening corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% in the month before decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of FEDFUNDS > 4.5% months, or FEDFUNDS decline sharply within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) above 135,000 coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength supports consumer and business confidence.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of PAYEMS > 135,000 events, or UNRATE remains below 4% during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (residential construction) of at least 10% predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak housing momentum reduces risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥10% over two consecutive months prior to decision
failure_condition: 20-day returns are non-negative in >60% of such HOUST declines, or GDP growth offsets construction weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) index below 95 coincides with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing signals deflationary pressure and short-term optimism.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative in >75% of INDPRO < 95 events, or broader GDP growth offsets the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 shows a positive 20-day forward return as lower unemployment is interpreted as a pro-equity policy environment.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >50% of such UNRATE periods, or inflation pressures override the signal.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% in the same month predict a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to dual demand weakness.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous and RSAFS < previous by ≥2%
failure_condition: 60-day returns are non-negative in >70% of such dual declines, or GDP recovers faster than retail sales.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in CPIAUCSL (CPI) above 198 for two months indicates rising inflation expectations, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >60% of such CPIAUCSL periods, or core inflation is lower than headline CPI.

mechanism_narrative: When both INDPRO and GDPC1 fall sequentially by more than 5% in the month prior to the decision, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 5-day forward return as market anticipates a supply-side shock recovery.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < prev by >5% and INDPRO < prev by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative in >80% of such events, or GDP and industrial production recover simultaneously within the window.
